title: A sharp entropy bound and the simplex inequality for isotropic constants

issues.location: Lemma sc:bounds / Appendix certificate.tex (scalar one-variable bounds)
issues.description: The whole argument depends on a table of one-variable rational bounds (p>0, |h0|<=.67 sqrt p, the lower bound p>=1/(7+a^2) for a<=0, the growth bound dlogM/dlogq>=m0, and the interval tables). I did not audit the appendix's tail estimates line by line. Instead I re-checked the bounds independently in high precision on a grid over [-30,30], and the authors' exact-rational verifier passes. The bound p>=1/(7+a^2) is very tight: the slack is about 7e-6 near its worst point, so the tail analysis there carries real weight. I found no failure.
issues.evidence: p(a) >= (7+a^2)^{-1} for a<=0; my grid check gives min slack ~7.3e-6. M'/(Md) - m0 >= 0.0022 on the grid.

coverage: I read all of main, introduction, transport, matrix, scalar, approximation, rigidity and geometry, and skimmed the appendix through its verifier. Hand-checked: the deficit identity (mat:deficit-exact); the Jacobian equation and its divergence form; the energy multiplier computation; the arithmetic-mean symmetrization identity, checked algebraically; the rearrangement step; the arithmetic-vs-log-average comparison and the hyperbolic identity; the exact match of the Taylor constants 1/16, 1/480 and 1/26880; the covariance completion C = W + E(2t - k^2 - sum K^2); the U representation; every term of Lemma mat:expansion, including the commutator and square-completion bookkeeping; P_T as a square; the 2x2 eigenvalue bound 1+s/8; the block Cauchy-Schwarz and weighted completion with pseudoinverses; all arithmetic in the absorption proof (minorant, .689, .027, F0 tangent and sqrt bounds, H rho u = omega); and the final chaos polynomial, factorization confirmed in sympy. I also checked the normalization degree argument, the Moreau/mollifier approximation, the compactness in the equality case, the linear-Jacobian commutation lemma and the cone reduction. Independent numeric checks: the scalar identities af - f' = 2t - k^2 - b^2 - 1 and f'' = l h_*; all one-variable bounds on a grid over [-30,30] at 500 digits; and the full two-eigenvalue Proposition mat:scalar-pair, tested directly as a 3x3 PSD condition on pairs from a grid over [-25,25]. It holds with normalized margin of about 0.027. The paper's verify_scalar.py prints ALL CHECKS PASSED.
main_claim: For every log-concave density f on R^m, h(f) >= m + (1/2) log det Cov(f), with equality exactly for affine images of products of one-sided exponentials. Through the exponential density on the cone over K, this gives the strong isotropic constant conjecture: L_K <= (n!)^{1/n} / ((n+1)^{(n+1)/(2n)} sqrt(n+2)), with equality only for simplices.
